verdicts.tldr: a realm the changed package reaches is dropped from the comment whenever the same PR also touches gnoweb
verdicts.details: isSeed() at comment.go:157 returns true for any of the four gnowebSeedRealms as soon as Plan.Gnoweb is set, and the indirect loop at :68 skips it, so membership in the seed list, not the reason the realm is in Plan.Realms, decides whether it is listed. BuildPlan puts gno.land/r/gnoland/home in Plan.Realms because it imports the changed gno.land/p/moul/dynreplacer/v0 (plan.go:236-247), gnodev renders it and Index lists it, and the comment names no realm but the changed one. Shots does not cover the gap: main.go:148-152 fills plan.Shots only when len(plan.ChangedRealms)==0, so a PR with a changed realm alongside gets an empty shotGrid. The reviewer is told the PR affects realm sources and is never shown the realm the change actually reaches. Fix: decide the skip on why the realm is in Plan.Realms, skipping a seed only when nothing changed reaches it, instead of on membership in gnowebSeedRealms.
verdicts.evidence: judge-66 on the real examples/ tree, changed = gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/app.go + examples/gno.land/p/moul/dynreplacer/v0/gnomod.toml + examples/gno.land/r/demo/counter/gnomod.toml: 'Mode=both Gnoweb=true ChangedRealms=[gno.land/r/demo/counter] ChangedPkgs=[gno.land/p/moul/dynreplacer/v0] Realms=[gno.land/r/demo/counter gno.land/r/docs/security_patterns gno.land/r/gnoland/blog gno.land/r/gnoland/boards2/v0 gno.land/r/gnoland/home]' and the emitted body carries only '- [`gno.land/r/demo/counter`](https://example.test/pr-1/r/demo/counter/)'. Differential in the same tree: drop the gnoweb file and keep the identical package change and TestProbeNoGnoweb logs 'Gnoweb=false Mode=realms Realms=[gno.land/r/gnoland/home]' with 'comment mentions home=true'. The Gnoweb flag alone is what hides the realm. The finder's own TestCommentDropsAffectedSeedRealm reruns FAIL with the same shape.
verdicts.verify_by: cd misc/gnopreview && go test -run TestCommentDropsAffectedSeedRealm (artifact below): BuildPlan on a fixture where r/gnoland/home imports the changed p/x/base/v0 plus a gnoweb file yields Mode=both, Realms=[gno.land/r/gnoland/home], and Comment() output contains no /r/gnoland/home link | `go test -run TestReachB5CommentHidesIndirectSeedRealm -v ./...` in misc/gnopreview with the artifact copied in: it builds the plan from the real tree and asserts every rendered realm is named in the comment | Comment(&Plan{Gnoweb: true, ChangedRealms: []string{"gno.land/r/x/leaf"}, Realms: []string{"gno.land/r/gnoland/home", "gno.land/r/x/leaf"}, Pairs: []ShotPair{{Realm: "gno.land/r/x/leaf", After: "_shots/a.png", URL: "r/x/leaf/"}}}, base, pr) and grep the output for r/gnoland/home | go test -run TestClaimAffectedSeedRealmIsUnlisted

verdicts.tldr: changed realms the cap dropped are posted as links to pages the preview never rendered
verdicts.details: plan.go:256-259 truncates the combined realm list at maxRealms and leaves Plan.ChangedRealms untouched; the stable sort above it only guarantees changed realms come first, which stops helping once there are more of them than the cap. comment.go:60-64 then emits one link per ChangedRealm with source and help tabs, so every changed realm past the cap gets a https://<pages>/r/.../ URL the crawler never wrote. examples/gno.land/r holds 58 realm directories against a default cap of 25, so one gnomod.toml or gno fmt sweep is enough. The reviewer clicks a link the comment presents exactly like the working ones and lands on a 404, with nothing saying which of the 58 are real. Fix: build the changed-realm list from the intersection with Plan.Realms, or give the cap a floor that never truncates below len(ChangedRealms).
verdicts.evidence: judge-67 on the real tree, every examples/gno.land/r gnomod.toml as changed at the default cap: 'changed files=58 ChangedRealms=58 Realms=25 Dropped=33 cap=25' then '33 changed realm(s) linked but never rendered, e.g. https://example.test/pr-1/r/gov/dao/treasury/test/v0/ for gno.land/r/gov/dao/treasury/test/v0'. The finder's TestCommentLinksUnrenderedChangedRealms reruns FAIL at cap 2 with 'ChangedRealms=[gno.land/r/x/a1 gno.land/r/x/a2 gno.land/r/x/a3] Realms=[gno.land/r/x/a1 gno.land/r/x/a2] Dropped=1'.
verdicts.verify_by: cd misc/gnopreview && go test -run TestCommentLinksUnrenderedChangedRealms (artifact below): BuildPlan with three changed realms and maxRealms=2, then check each ChangedRealm absent from Realms against the comment text | cp the artifact into misc/gnopreview and run `go test -run TestReachB5 -v ./...`: TestReachB5TreeWideChangeOutrunsTheCap feeds every examples/gno.land/r gnomod.toml as changed at the default cap, TestReachB5CommentLinksUnrenderedChangedRealms does it on the fake repo at cap 1 | cd misc/gnopreview && go test -run TestCatalogChangedRealmsSurviveTheCap -v . | cp tests/b10-lines-cap-drops-changed-realms_test.go misc/gnopreview/b10_cap_test.go && cd misc/gnopreview && go test -run TestB10CapDropsChangedRealms -v ./...

verdicts.tldr: the cap note tells the reviewer the changed realms were kept in the run where the cap dropped them
verdicts.details: The note at comment.go:86 states 'the changed realms are always kept' unconditionally, and plan.go:253-259 does not keep them: the stable sort puts changed realms first, then the truncation cuts the whole slice at maxRealms with no floor, so a diff with more changed realms than the cap loses the surplus. The note is the only thing the reviewer has to tell a missing realm from a rendered one, and it says the opposite of what happened, so it reads the dropped realms as indirect dependents that were not worth rendering. Measured on the real tree, 33 of 58 changed realms were dropped under that sentence. Fix: derive the note from the run, naming how many of the dropped realms were changed, or hold the invariant by flooring the cap at len(ChangedRealms).
verdicts.evidence: judge-67 TestJudge67CapNoteContradictsTheDrop on every examples/gno.land/r gnomod.toml at the default cap: 'changed realms dropped by the cap=33 Dropped=33' then 'cap dropped 33 of 58 changed realms, yet the comment says "the changed realms are always kept"'. The finder's TestB5DroppedChangedRealmAgainstTheNote reruns FAIL at cap 2 with the dropped realm's link sitting above the note in the same body.
